**Caching in Computer Systems**

Caching is one of the most important ideas in computer systems. It is a technique used to store copies of frequently accessed data in a faster, more accessible location so that future requests can be served more quickly. Although caching appears in many different forms—from processor caches to web caches, database caches, and content delivery networks—the underlying principle is the same: reduce the cost of accessing data by keeping useful data closer to the consumer. In modern computing, caching is essential because it helps bridge the gap between the speed of computation and the speed of data retrieval.

At its core, caching exists because not all storage is equal. A computer system contains many layers of storage, each with different characteristics. Registers are extremely fast but very small.
